description: Team UnknownX is a passionate group of developers, researchers, and space enthusiasts building innovative solutions with AI, software, GIS, data, and UI/UX for NASA Space Apps 2026. Let’s explore Mars together!
summary:
MarsWay is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform developed to address the NASA Space Apps Challenge, “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map.” It combines a 2D GIS map, 3D Mars Globe, first-person Astronaut EVA simulation, and an explainable route planner to help users explore Martian terrain and understand environmental conditions.

The route planner compares Shortest, Safest, and Science-priority routes by considering factors such as distance, elevation, slope, terrain conditions, potential hazards, and scientific value. MarsWay also features a multilingual local assistant supporting English, Bangla, and Banglish, along with offline access to locally available features.

By combining multiple NASA and USGS planetary datasets in one interactive platform, MarsWay makes complex scientific information easier to understand and explore. It aims to support planetary science education, research, and future Mars exploration planning through an accessible and transparent educational prototype.
details:
MarsWay – An Interplanetary Survival Guide for Mars

How We Addressed the Challenge

NASA's challenge, “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map,” encourages participants to explore how Martian geographical and scientific information can support understanding and planning for future surface exploration.

We addressed this challenge by developing MarsWay as a unified platform that connects planetary maps, scientific datasets, environmental context, and simulated exploration scenarios.

Instead of presenting Mars information as separate maps and scientific documents, MarsWay allows users to explore the planet through multiple connected experiences. The 2D GIS Map provides geographical context, the 3D Globe offers a global perspective, and the Astronaut EVA simulation demonstrates a first-person exploration scenario.

Our explainable route planner further addresses the challenge by comparing different exploration priorities. It evaluates factors such as distance, elevation, slope, terrain conditions, potential hazards, and scientific value to generate route suggestions.

Through this approach, MarsWay demonstrates how publicly available planetary science information can be organized into an interactive environment for understanding Martian exploration challenges.

How MarsWay Works

MarsWay provides several connected features that allow users to explore Mars and understand different aspects of the Martian environment.

1. Interactive 2D Mars GIS Map

The 2D GIS Map provides an interactive geographical view of Mars. Users can explore planetary locations, geographical features, mission sites, coordinates, and available scientific map layers.

It includes terrain-related information and map visualization using resources such as MOLA elevation data, THEMIS imagery, and available planetary basemap layers. Users can examine different locations and understand their geographical context through the map interface.

2. Interactive 3D Mars Globe

The 3D Mars Globe provides an interactive global representation of the planet using Three.js. Users can rotate and explore Mars, examine planetary features, and view important geographical locations and mission markers.

It complements the 2D map by providing a more immersive perspective of the Martian surface. The globe also includes planetary visualization elements such as Phobos, Deimos, and an Earth scale comparison.

3. Astronaut EVA Simulation

The Astronaut Extravehicular Activity (EVA) View provides a first-person simulated Mars exploration experience through a helmet-inspired interface.

Users can move across the virtual Martian surface, examine geological features, collect virtual samples, and access exploration-related information. The interface includes environmental telemetry, geological scanning, sample collection, and forward hazard scanning.

This feature demonstrates how an astronaut might interact with environmental and geographical information during a simulated surface exploration activity.

4. Explainable Route Planner

The Explainable Route Planner is one of the core decision-support features of MarsWay. It compares three route strategies:

  • Shortest Route: Prioritizes reducing travel distance.
  • Safest Route: Prioritizes terrain suitability and lower potential hazard exposure.
  • Science-priority Route: Considers scientific value and interesting exploration targets.

The route-planning logic considers multiple factors, including distance, elevation, slope, terrain conditions, potential hazards, soil trafficability, and scientific value.

The system provides route comparisons, waypoints, hazard context, and explanations of why different routes may be preferable under different priorities. This helps users understand that the shortest route is not necessarily the most suitable route for every exploration objective.

5. Ask MarsWay – Multilingual Local Assistant

Ask MarsWay is a local assistant designed to help users access information and interact with supported application features.

It supports English, Bangla, and Banglish through local datasets, intent matching, and deterministic application logic. Its core local functions do not require a remote AI service or external API key.

This approach makes the assistant more accessible to users with different language preferences while supporting the project's offline-first design.

6. Voice Navigation

MarsWay also includes browser-based voice navigation using the Web Speech API. It provides an additional interaction method through supported voice commands that trigger selected application functions.

This feature makes the interface more interactive and demonstrates an alternative way to navigate the platform.

7. Data Transparency and Scientific Provenance

MarsWay distinguishes different types of information to help users understand how displayed results should be interpreted.

It uses five provenance categories:

  • Observed: Information originating from instrument observations or source records.
  • Historical: Previously collected mission or mapping information.
  • Derived: Values calculated from coordinates, geometry, or other source information.
  • Modeled: Results generated through scientific or engineering approximations.
  • Simulated: Information or scenarios generated for interactive demonstration.

This approach helps users distinguish scientific observations from calculations, estimates, and simulated experiences.

8. Scientific Map Layers and Environmental Overlays

MarsWay provides different scientific visualization layers to help users understand the Martian surface and its environmental context.

Available visualization capabilities include:

  • Viking surface imagery.
  • THEMIS infrared visualization.
  • MOLA shaded-relief and elevation information.
  • Atmospheric pressure and temperature visualization.
  • Regional environmental information.
  • Seasonal dust-storm simulation with haze, wind vectors, and optical-depth visualization.
  • Mission and landing-site information.
  • Elevation-data availability and resolution visualization.

Users can activate selected overlays, adjust their visibility, and compare different types of information within the same geographical workspace.

How We Developed This Project

We developed MarsWay as a browser-based application using a modular approach. Its different components combine planetary data visualization, local processing, route-planning logic, and interactive user experiences.

Our development process included the following stages:

  1. Research and Data Collection: We explored publicly available NASA and USGS planetary resources to identify useful geographical, geological, and environmental information for Mars exploration.
  2. Interface Development: We developed the main application interface and organized its features into accessible sections for planetary exploration.
  3. 2D and 3D Visualization: We implemented the interactive Mars GIS Map using Leaflet and the 3D Mars Globe using Three.js.
  4. Astronaut Simulation: We developed a first-person EVA experience with a helmet-inspired interface, exploration controls, and environmental information.
  5. Route Planning: We implemented local route-planning and decision logic to compare different exploration priorities using terrain-related and scientific factors.
  6. Assistant and Voice Interaction: We developed Ask MarsWay using local intent matching and application logic, while browser voice capabilities support selected voice commands.
  7. Offline Support: We implemented Service Workers and local data caching to make locally available features and cached resources accessible without a continuous internet connection.

The result is an integrated prototype that connects scientific information with interactive exploration and mission-planning demonstrations.

Development Methodology: Agile Model

We followed an Agile-inspired development approach to build MarsWay through iterative and incremental development. Instead of developing the entire platform at once, we divided the project into smaller modules, including the 2D GIS Map, 3D Mars Globe, Astronaut EVA Simulation, Route Planner, and Ask MarsWay Assistant.

Each module was developed, tested, and refined progressively before being integrated into the main platform. Team members collaborated on different responsibilities, while continuous testing and feedback helped us identify issues, improve functionality, and refine the user experience.

This iterative approach allowed us to adapt to technical challenges, improve individual features, and gradually develop MarsWay into an integrated Mars exploration and mission-planning platform.

Hope to Achieve

Our vision is to make MarsWay a useful educational and research-oriented platform for understanding the challenges of future Mars exploration.

We hope to:

  • Make planetary science information more accessible to students, educators, and researchers.
  • Demonstrate how multiple planetary datasets can be combined into one interactive exploration platform.
  • Improve understanding of Martian geography, terrain conditions, and environmental information.
  • Support educational demonstrations of astronaut EVA activities and exploration scenarios.
  • Encourage the development of accessible, multilingual, and offline-first planetary exploration tools.

Ultimately, we hope MarsWay will inspire more people to explore planetary science and understand the challenges involved in future human missions to Mars.

Highlighted Features

  • Interactive 2D Mars GIS Map – Explores Martian geographical features, locations, and scientific map layers.
  • 3D Mars Globe – Provides an interactive global view of Mars and important planetary features.
  • Astronaut EVA Simulation – Demonstrates first-person exploration through a helmet-inspired interface.
  • Explainable Route Planner – Compares Shortest, Safest, and Science-priority routes.
  • Ask MarsWay Assistant – Supports English, Bangla, and Banglish through local application logic.
  • Voice Navigation – Supports interaction with selected application functions through voice commands.
  • Environmental Information – Presents available Martian environmental and scientific context.
  • Offline-First Support – Keeps locally available features and cached resources accessible without continuous internet connectivity.

Benefits

MarsWay makes complex planetary science information easier to explore and understand. Its integrated approach provides several benefits:

  • For Students and Educators: Offers an interactive learning environment for understanding planetary geography, geology, and Mars exploration.
  • For Researchers: Provides an accessible interface for exploring publicly available planetary datasets and examining terrain-related information.
  • For Exploration Studies: Demonstrates how distance, elevation, slope, terrain conditions, and scientific value can influence route selection.
  • For General Users: Makes Mars exploration more engaging through maps, 3D visualization, and simulated astronaut experiences.
  • For Accessibility: Supports English, Bangla, and Banglish interaction through a local assistant.
  • For Offline Use: Provides access to locally available features and cached resources without requiring continuous internet connectivity.

What Is the Intended Impact?

Our main goal is to bridge the gap between planetary science data and practical Mars exploration planning.

MarsWay aims to make publicly available planetary information easier to explore, understand, and apply in simulated exploration scenarios. It can support planetary science education, research demonstrations, and astronaut EVA training concepts.

By bringing multiple scientific resources into one interactive platform, we want to demonstrate how technology can make complex planetary information more understandable and useful.

The project also highlights the importance of transparent data interpretation by distinguishing between direct observations, historical records, derived information, modeled results, and simulated experiences.

Tools and Technologies Used

MarsWay was developed as a browser-based application using the following technologies:

Programming Languages

  • TypeScript
  • JavaScript
  • HTML
  • CSS

Frontend and Frameworks

  • React
  • Vite
  • Modern CSS

Mapping and Visualization

  • Leaflet
  • Three.js

Backend

  • Node.js
  • Express

Offline Support

  • Service Workers
  • Local Data Caching

Local Processing

  • TypeScript-based datasets
  • Route calculation logic
  • Local decision-making algorithms

These technologies work together to provide interactive maps, 3D planetary visualization, simulated exploration, local assistant functions, and route comparisons.

How Is the Project Creative?

MarsWay brings several different exploration experiences together instead of presenting Mars information as separate maps, images, and scientific documents.

Its creative aspects include:

  • Connected Exploration Experiences: Combines a 2D planetary map, interactive 3D Globe, and first-person astronaut simulation.
  • Multiple Route Priorities: Demonstrates how different exploration goals can produce different route recommendations.
  • Explainable Decision Support: Provides route comparisons and contextual explanations rather than presenting only a single result.
  • Multilingual Local Assistant: Supports English, Bangla, and Banglish without requiring a remote AI service for its core local functions.
  • Offline-First Design: Keeps locally available application features and cached resources accessible when continuous internet access is unavailable.
  • Data Transparency: Uses labels such as Observed, Historical, Derived, Modeled, and Simulated to help users understand the nature of the information being presented.

By combining these elements, MarsWay offers a more engaging and accessible approach to exploring planetary science information.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

During development, our team considered several factors to make MarsWay useful, understandable, and transparent.

  • Terrain and Elevation: Considered geographical conditions, elevation, and slope when developing terrain-related exploration features.
  • Distance and Route Selection: Considered route length and different exploration priorities.
  • Potential Hazards: Included terrain-related risk context and hazard information in the route-planning experience.
  • Scientific Value: Considered geological features and scientific targets when designing the Science-priority route option.
  • Data Reliability: Considered source quality, coverage, historical context, and limitations of available datasets.
  • Accessibility: Focused on understandable interfaces and multilingual interaction.
  • Offline Availability: Considered access to local features and previously cached resources.
  • Transparency: Distinguished between observed, historical, derived, modeled, and simulated information.

Not every Martian location has the same level of scientific coverage. Therefore, we considered the limitations of available information and aimed to communicate the nature of the data clearly.

Design, Development and Video Showcase

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/ahsanur-official/Interplanetary-Survival-Guide-Martian-Map

240 Seconds Project Demonstration Video: https://youtu.be/zjjztrTMbhI

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

AI-assisted tools supported different stages of MarsWay's brainstorming, planning, documentation, development, debugging, and creative workflow.

  1. ChatGPT: Assisted with project understanding, ideation, technical explanations, documentation, and development planning.
  2. Claude: Supported brainstorming, research organization, and reviewing development approaches.
  3. Gemini: Assisted with research, multimodal content development, and creative tasks.
  4. Google AI Studio: Supported early project structuring and development assistance.
  5. Codex: Assisted with coding, implementation, and debugging.
  6. Google Flow: Used for AI-assisted video creation and creative visual production.
  7. Omni Flash: Used for video-related creative work.

These tools supported our development workflow. However, MarsWay's core mapping, route-planning, and local assistant functionalities are implemented through application code, local datasets, and deterministic logic rather than relying on a remote AI service for every operation.

Disclaimer

MarsWay is an independent educational and research-oriented prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It is not an official NASA product or an endorsed NASA navigation system.

Its route suggestions, environmental interpretations, and exploration scenarios are based on available datasets, application logic, and modeled or simulated information. They are intended for educational and demonstration purposes only and are not certified for real astronaut or rover navigation or safety-critical mission decisions.
